intent: A naturalist slowing the clock down: the age, how it was read, how slowly the animal grows, then the date that makes it real.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Which of these animals lives the LONGEST?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Which of these animals lives the longest?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat
lines.text: Bowhead whale, Giant tortoise, or Greenland shark?
The Greenland shark. A single female was dated at roughly 400 years old.

lines.direction: ease back over the North Atlantic; three columns rise — the shark's twice the whale's; the whale sticker on 'beats', the eye sticker on 'lens'
lines.text: That beats the bowhead whale at 200, and any tortoise. Its age was read in the lens of its eye.

lines.direction: push north-east into the Arctic sea between Greenland and Svalbard; the ruler sticker on 'grows', the Arctic tag on 'water', the snowflake sticker; from 'adult' a counter creeps to 150
lines.text: It grows about 1 centimetre a year in freezing water, and is not an adult until around 150.

lines.direction: drift back to Greenland's coast; the shark sticker on 'swimming'; a SHARK / USA split on 'born' — 1744 against 1776; the Greenland highlight pulses on 'existed'
lines.text: So a shark off Greenland today may have been born before the United States existed.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
